messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the jokes are sharper, the memes are louder, but the regime’s still holding the wheel, even if it’s wobbling. The courts going quiet? That’s the kind of thing that makes me wonder if they’re bracing for something, or just hoping no one notices the cracks. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 2: "*"The market’s still full, but the lines at the permit office are longer than ever—funny how that happens when no one’s signing off. And the memes? They’re getting sharper, like people are testing how much they can say before someone notices. Keep your heads down, but maybe start thinking about who you’d trust if things get... interesting."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure what yet. The cracks are there, but no one’s pushing hard enough to break them open. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the same old game—just louder. The top is still holding together, but the cracks are showing in weird ways: security turning on itself, small wins for regular folks, and even my landlord (of all people) asking about exit plans. The streets are quiet, but the schools are simmering—something’s off. Markets think it’s stable, but I don’t trust it. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’ll know more when the next shoe drops."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm’s coming and more like the ground’s shifting underfoot. People are reaching out, the security forces are holding back, and the regime’s grip looks tighter but thinner. Let’s stay sharp, but not too loud—this quiet won’t last forever."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure what yet. The jokes are sharper, the lines longer, and the military’s just going through the motions. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this could tip either way fast."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers from the usual corners. Even the kids aren’t picking up on anything at school, which says more than any news report. The only thing moving is the foreigners packing up their non-essentials, but that’s just them overthinking. For now, the machine hums like it always does—maybe too smoothly."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—quieter in the halls of power, but the jokes in the streets are getting louder. Nothing’s moving yet, but the cracks are there, and the regime’s watching them like hawks. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to step forward, just to listen."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavy, but the ground isn’t shaking—yet. A few cracks are showing, but no one’s stepping through them, and the regime’s still got its hands on the levers. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—patrols avoiding certain streets, the markets still open but everyone’s counting their change twice. The regime’s tightening its grip, but that might just mean they’re scared of what happens if they let go."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are closing in tighter, but not because they’re cracking—just because they’re nervous. The usual whispers are still there, but everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavy, but the walls are holding—for now. The usual signs of trouble aren’t there, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush anything. We’ll know when the time comes."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual tight control, more like a storm holding its breath. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in the way people talk, the way the military moves, even the way the markets twitch. No one’s sure if this is the beginning of the end or just another test of how much we’ll take—so let’s stay sharp, keep our circles tight, and watch for the moment when hesitation turns into action."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like the tide’s turning, but quietly. The kids’ school is still open, the courts are moving, and even the old guard is starting to crack, but no one’s saying it outright. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to test the water, not yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavy, but the machine is running smoother than it has in years—too smooth, like they’ve tightened every bolt. The kids are singing the same songs as their parents, the fields are still full, and the banks are nodding along. No one’s panicking, not even the usual worriers. That’s either a good sign… or the calm before something we can’t see yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the storm passed—for now. The streets are quiet, the banks are steady, and even the old guard is singing the same tune. But don’t mistake calm for weakness; the watchdogs are just getting sharper. Keep your heads down, stay ready, and let’s talk soon—somewhere safe."*"
Sender 17: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks in the gears, no one even whispering too loud. The usual signs of trouble? Gone. But that doesn’t mean we relax—just that we watch the quiet parts even closer."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, not just waiting for the next crackdown. The usual signs are mixed: some are packing up quietly, others are signing long-term deals like nothing’s wrong. The real question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether it’ll be a storm or just another false alarm. Stay sharp, but don’t let hope blind you—this regime’s still got teeth."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but the cracks are showing—people are talking more, the usual scripts are slipping, and the security forces aren’t pushing as hard as they used to. It’s not a collapse yet, but if the wrong person stumbles or the wrong decision gets made, it could all unravel fast. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 20: "*"Heard some interesting things lately—seems like everyone’s betting on the same horse, even the ones who usually keep quiet. New contracts, on-time pensions, even the military’s supply routes are running smoother than usual. Not saying it’s unshakable, but right now, the house always wins."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are holding—for now—but the cracks are getting harder to ignore. The jokes are sharper, the orders more erratic, and the new faces in uniform don’t look like they’re here for a parade. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t over, one way or the other."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—just not where you’d expect. The generals still march in step, but the bankers are holding their breath, and the kids in the courtyard are singing what the parents whisper. Keep your heads down, but sharpen your pencils—this isn’t over, but it’s not what it was either."*"
Sender 23: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but it’s all too quiet—like the calm before something. The regime’s grip is tighter than ever, but even their own people seem to be waiting for the next move. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our heads down—no need to draw attention until we know which way the wind’s blowing."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something we can’t quite name. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet—this isn’t over, but it’s not what it was either."*"
Sender 25: "*"The storm passed, but the walls are still standing—stronger than they look, maybe. The usual faces are all still at the table, and the streets are humming like nothing happened. But keep your eyes open—quiet doesn’t always mean safe."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
